🇲🇽🏭 <u>Mexico's AI Export Boom: Big Numbers, Thin Roots</u>

Banxico, via El Economista: computers, peripherals and electronic components explained 82% of the rise in Mexico's non-auto manufacturing exports from January 2024 to September 2026. Those exports grew 96.8%; non-transport manufacturing output grew 2.2%. Domestic value added in the two branches: just 15.9% to 27.1%. Banxico flags semiconductors and integrated circuits as where Mexico could capture more of the chain.

🇲🇽📊 <u>Unpaid Care Work: 24.3% of Mexico's GDP</u>

INEGI's satellite account puts unpaid domestic and care work at 8.7 trillion pesos, 24.3% of GDP, bigger than manufacturing (19.9%) or commerce (18.5%). Women produce 72.5% of it, 2.6 times men's share, worth 87,601 pesos per woman a year. In Chiapas and Guerrero it exceeds 50% of the local economy. The largest sector in the country has no payroll.

🇲🇽🏥 <u>12,750 Clinics, One Door for Everyone</u>

Mexico is readying 12,750 IMSS-Bienestar doctor's offices across 24 states for the universal health service starting January 2027: care for anyone, whether they hold IMSS, ISSSTE or IMSS-Bienestar. About 3,000 are already set up; 6,000 more open in January. Communities rehabbed them through La Clínica es Nuestra: 5,325 assemblies, nearly 200,000 people, money delivered straight to local committees. The hiring call drew 82,000 applications; 4,310 doctors and nurses are already assigned.

🇲🇽💜 <u>"Men for the Transformation": 12 Pledges Against Machismo</u>

Mexico's Secretariat of Women launched a national campaign aimed at men, not just victims. Secretary Laura Itzel Castillo: telling women where to go after an attack isn't enough if nothing stops the violence. The 12 commitments, drafted in workshops with men from different trades, include renouncing all violence, sharing care work, rejecting online groups that normalize aggression against women, and understanding power "as a service, not a form of oppression." They go to schools, workplaces and communities through the 16 Days of Activism ending December 10.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>G20 Is Not the "Last Chance," Sheinbaum Tells Trump</u>

Sheinbaum says her December meeting with Trump at the G20 in Miami is not a now-or-never moment for a tariff deal. Mexico wants the Section 232 tariffs on cars, steel and aluminum cut, and will only sign what benefits Mexico. Around 90 non-tariff barrier issues are already settled without touching sovereignty. Her reminder: Trump still has two years left in office, and there is always dialogue.
banner: G20: 'NOT THE LAST CHANCE' ON TARIFFS

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Mexico Files Formal Complaint Over DEA's Snitch Lines</u>

Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco delivered a formal complaint to US Ambassador Ronald Johnson over the DEA's WhatsApp and Signal tip lines inviting people in Sinaloa, and soon Jalisco, to inform on Mexican officials and politicians. Sheinbaum called it interference: security cooperation continues, but "tenemos que defender la soberanía." Johnson's reply: he'll check it. The agency that let 1.4 million fentanyl pills circulate in New Mexico now wants informant hotlines aimed at Mexican politics.
banner: DEA HOTLINES: FORMAL COMPLAINT TO US

🇲🇽🏥 <u>IMSS 2027: 49 Pesos of Every 100 Go to Pensions, 35 to Health</u>

IMSS will have a 1.8 trillion-peso budget in 2027, up 9.8% in real terms. Per El Economista, citing México Evalúa, 49 of every 100 pesos will pay pensions under the 1973 law and 35 will go to health care. In 2013 it was almost the reverse: 48 to health, 30 to pensions. Pensions have outspent medical care since 2019. Under the law, the federal government funds those 1973-law pensions.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Taxpayers Even Paid for Lorenzo Córdova's Wedding</u>

An internal electoral-institute document shows that on October 30, 2000, the IFE paid Lorenzo Córdova a "marriage dowry" of nearly 40,000 pesos in public money. The perk wasn't scrapped until 2017. The same Córdova whose INE turns up in the USAIDgate files.

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>Sheinbaum's Family-Justice Reform: Faster Adoptions, No More Hostage Divorces</u>

Sheinbaum sent Congress a reform of the National Code of Civil and Family Procedures. Between 25,000 and 35,000 children live in care centers, and 7 in 10 could be adopted if it weren't for red tape. The reform cuts the adoption suitability certificate from 90 to 45 days and lets judges check SAT and bank records so fathers can't hide income to dodge child support. It also orders protection within 24 hours against vicarious violence. "As if justice could be divided," said Arturo Zaldívar, "we are forcing children to live with their abusers."

🇲🇽🗳️ <u>INE Hands Its Stage to Somos "Experts" to Attack Morena's Majority</u>

In the middle of the electoral-materials contracts scandal, Mexico's INE hosted a forum on proportional representation and billed José Woldenberg, Jacqueline Peschard and Mariana Calderón as "independent specialists." Contralínea reports Woldenberg advises the right-wing party Somos and Calderón sits on its advisory council. Hours earlier, PAN's Ricardo Anaya had threatened to boycott the 2027 elections unless the plurinominal rules change. The "neutral experts" repeated the same script.
